what: The material library (L1 B2): every lit surface's cel class, the only place a class's numbers live. cel: the per-material uniforms of shaders/cel.gdshaderinc (band, mid, form, spec, nmap, ink, rim_k; see its header); sheen: a metal's second, sky-colored band (rule 6) where a shader carries it; edge: the crowd's own rim (width in 1-n.v, step). paint: B3's painted-block parameters, the colors measured from the boards by tools/style/board_measure.py (boxes in board pixels with optional Oklab masks; re-run it to re-measure): paint.lit as painted on the board (lit paint), paint.albedo (v2, B3r2) the board's samples over the game's own response to each class (tools/look/calib.py: the swatch row at albedo 1 under the day and night rigs, solved per channel, then iterated on the swatches redrawn in it). B3 paints from albedo. shaders: each adopting shader's default class (its CEL_* defines must equal it: godot/tests/MaterialLibraryTests.cs). assign: material to class, first match wins (shader path, material name and asset path as .NET regexes; all given must match). exclude: what is not converted, by design.

lights.what: B2r2: the boards' own light, divided out of paint.lit to give paint.albedo (tools/style/board_measure.py's docstring). Each LB panel's E is the mean linear color of its lit neutral references (gray setts, limewashed plaster), the lit side of each box (pixels at or over its median luminance), scaled to luminance 1: the light's color divided out, its strength left to the rig (B4). A board row with refs of its own takes the nearest panel by measurement (match); the others name theirs by the board's own label. First row that holds a box's center wins.
